data.gender_notes: Jacquie is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Western Christianity, the name Jacqueline is a derivative from the masculine name Jacob, which means 'supplanter' or 'he who follows after'. In the Old Testament, Jacob was a deceiver, but he was also a man of faith who was loved by God. This name carries the traits of determination, courage, and faith. The name Jacquie carries the meaning “Supplanter, one who follows after” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Jacquie usually hope their child will grow to embody supplanter, one who follows after and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name with a rich spiritual heritage, carrying the determination and faith of the Old Testament character Jacob.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jacquie total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jacqueline was popularized in the Middle Ages by Christina de Pisan, a woman who wrote a book in honor of the Virgin Mary called the "Book of the City of Ladies". This book celebrated the virtues of women and the name Jacqueline became a name for noblewomen and noble births.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Jacqueline carries the spiritual traits of determination, courage, and faith, as seen in the biblical Jacob. As a Christian name, Jacqueline can be a reminder of the strength and resilience of the women of the faith, who continue to follow after God despite adversity and challenges.
